newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech minister warns C/A deficit near crisis-paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech minister warns C/A deficit near crisis-paper.

text.p: The Czech current account deficit could reach crisis proportions next year if the current trend continues, Industry Minister Vladimir Dlouhy was quoted as saying in the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny on Thursday.
In the first half of 1996, the deficit widened to $1.7 billion, more than double a year ago's $723 million deficit.
Prime Minster Vaclav Klaus has forecast a deficit of around 5.7 percent of GDP this year.

"The Czech Republic will have a current account deficit in the next years...It has been rising and should it continue at this speed, it will reach a critical point in the next year," the paper quoted Dlouhy as saying.
To avoid crisis, Dlouhy said a slowdown in wage growth to spur a fall in domestic demand were necessary.

"In my opinion, mainly internal changes would help us in the next year such as a slowdown of rising wages and thus, a slowdown of domestic demand. This would also support savings by higher interest rates and dividends," he said.
